articles.body: The first round of Brazil’s presidential election on Sunday pits two well-known names in the political ring: Lula vs. Bolsonaro. But it’s not former president Jair Bolsonaro facing off against the incumbent head of state – it’s his eldest son, Flavio Bolsonaro. He’s less charismatic than his father but just as ideologically radical as the family patriarch.

articles.body: In a week that’s seen the heroism of the captain, crew and passengers on board FlyDubai flight 1073 heralded, eye witnesses report seeing the co-pilot trying to kill the pilot and destroying the cockpit controls in order to crash the plane. Despite being stabbed repeatedly, Captan Smit Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to overwhelm the suspect and regain control of the aircraft after its rapid descent of more than 14,000 feet in 30 seconds. They prevented a 9/11-style catastrophe, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said.

Despite Michael Olise’s splendid free kick, the French were quickly overpowered by a clinical Italian side.

The TPLF has been fighting against federal forces and pro-government militias since September 23 and launching attacks into neighbouring states, raising fears of an all-out civil war similar to that of 2020-2022.

articles.body: It's been 18 days since we first reported on isolated cases of schools protests at a high school in Rennes in Brittany, in Caen in Normandy and Villeneueve d'Asque on the suburbs of Lille. The complaints were similar in theme, overloaded timetables, staffing problems, poor facilities. It spread to Saint Denis and Creteil on the outskirts of Paris days later, one interview with the students was sen 1.4 million times on TikTok. It gathered pace, and morphed into what we've seen throughout the week, hundreds of protests, some peaceful, some with deeply distressing scenes, beyond the make shift barricades, a school in Nantes set off fire, firefighters forced out of the vehicle in Marseille and the fire engine set alight, scroll your socials itt's hard to miss some of the uglier scenes, a female police officer being attacked on the ground as youths shouted kill her. Where is it heading, and what has it become? Urban violence says the government, accusing agitators linked to the hard left exploiting geenuine concerns for political ends ahead of the election. Which La France Insoumise denies saying they favour no violent means of action. Today in Spotlight, we discuss this with Jean Remi Girard, a teacher in Asnieres in the north of Paris, and the President of the National Union des Lycees and Colleges, covering education workers from primary schools to college, 7 until 18.
articles.headline: French Unrest: Are we witnessing a new 'Yellow Vests' movement?

articles.body: RAPE LAW LOOPHOLE: Gov. Kathy Hochul vowed today to close a loophole embedded in state rape law around voluntary intoxification as she laced into Cornell University police and a local district attorney for their handling of a 2024 gang rape allegation. Under current law, proving sexual assault is difficult if a victim voluntarily consumed alcohol or drugs. Individuals cannot consent “by reason of being mentally disabled or mentally incapacitated,” which generally applies to involuntary consumption of drugs or alcohol. Hochul said she would work with lawmakers “early” to change the law when they return to Albany in January. “Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape,” Hochul told reporters at her Midtown Manhattan office. “Period. I support closing this loophole and will work with the New York State Legislature to accomplish this.” The State Senate has consistently attempted to do just that through legislation , but the Assembly has yet to bring the bill up for a vote. Hochul also appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor on the case. Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff has agreed to an independent review. The plaintiff, a former Cornell student, alleged in a lawsuit that several men raped her at the Chi Phi house after coercing her into consuming drugs. The case attracted national attention after the student-run Cornell Daily Sun broke the story . The woman, identified in court papers as Jane Doe, told the Cornell campus police that she was “100 percent confident that she had been raped,” according to a transcript of her conversation with investigators . But that part of her account, Hochul noted, was omitted from the materials Cornell police sent to Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who declined to pursue charges without interviewing the woman. “In what world would the police learn from the victim that she had been literally gang-raped while intoxicated by five men in a fraternity house and not elevate those allegations to the district attorney?” she said. “In what world does the district attorney not even interview her or anyone else involved, or even request the full transcript?” Earlier this week, James expressed solidarity with Jane Doe on social media . When asked about her decision to affirm the allegation, she declined to comment. Rebecca Valli, a Cornell spokesperson, said the university agrees with the governor’s decision. “We fully support the appointment of a special prosecutor and efforts to change New York State’s rape law and are committed to an independent external review of all aspects of how Cornell has handled this case,” Valli said in a statement. Van Houten, the Tompkins County prosecutor, said in a statement today that “we were not provided the full picture by the university.” — Madina Touré MARK YOUR CALENDAR: Join POLITICO’s New York Outlook: Affordability, Industry & The Economy on Oct. 14 for live conversations about the business and policy decisions being made today — from City Hall to the State Capitol — that will shape the city’s economic future. The lineup includes New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin, New York City Economic Development Corp. CEO Anthony Shorris, Partnership for NYC CEO Steven Fulop, Citizens Budget Commission President Andrew Rein, Charles H. Revson Foundation President Maria Torres-Springer, and more. Register now to attend in person or watch the livestream . From the Capitol SPACE JAM: The fledgling United States Space Force is trying to find a home for its academy. State Sen. James Skoufis wants to make it so in the Hudson Valley, proposing that the recently formed military branch select Stewart International Airport. “New York Stewart International Airport would be an exceptional site for this project. It offers existing aerospace infrastructure — including one of the few runways in the country designated for space shuttle landings — alongside significant on-site development opportunities,” Skoufis wrote in a letter to Hochul this week. The Democratic state lawmaker is seizing on a NASA-led effort seeking input from governors interested in hosting or sponsoring the academy in their state. Skoufis wants to build interest in having the academy placed in New York, where some officials are trying to encourage growth in the space sector. “We built the Apollo lunar landers and refined the optics for every major NASA telescope,” said Patrick Chase, co-founder of Empire Space, a non-profit promoting economic opportunities in space. “The Empire State is the best location for the United States Space Academy, continuing our bold legacy as a pioneer of the American Space Age." — Nick Reisman BLAKEMAN’S VAGUE VOWS: Republican Bruce Blakeman has spent this year’s gubernatorial campaign focused on attacks — leaving serious questions about what he’d actually do if elected governor. With a month to go until Election Day, the Nassau County executive doesn’t have a policy section on his website. On the campaign trail, he’s opted against making detailed policy prescriptions in favor of going after Hochul and Mayor Zohran Mamdani. When asked in August about his plan to reign in housing costs — a top concern among New York voters — Blakeman pivoted immediately to ideology: “It’s not through socialism.” “That’s a failed system,” he said at the time. “Mamdani the Commie and Comrade Kathy, they have this completely backwards because wherever they’ve instituted socialism it’s been making people miserable.” Blakeman’s policy agenda has focused on two major issues — massive tax cuts and an immediate 50 percent reduction in utility bills on his first day in office. But neither plan has been backed up by accounting that might suggest they’re plausible. His campaign declined repeated requests to release a plan detailing the cuts needed for the tax breaks. “It strikes me as very back-of-the-envelope,” said E.J. McMahon, who helped author former Republican Gov. George Pataki’s tax cut proposal. “A damp, coffee-stained envelope.” George Marlin, a former Conservative Party mayoral nominee in New York City and ex-director of the Nassau Interim Finance Authority, took such criticism a step further, writing in a Times Union op-ed today that Blakeman’s record on Long Island suggests he is not “fiscally skilled enough to merit a promotion to the state’s top job.” “As county executive, Blakeman has done nothing to restrain spending,” Marlin wrote. “Despite his misleading campaign rhetoric, he has never cut a penny in county taxes.” Blakeman’s campaign did not respond to Marlin’s attacks. Read more from Bill Mahoney in POLITICO here .  TROOPER ONE’S SUIT: A federal judge this week dismissed one of the retaliation claims against ex-Gov. Andrew Cuomo in a lawsuit filed by a former member of his State Police security detail. U.S. District Court Judge LaShann DeArcy Hall determined that because the alleged retaliation occurred in February 2022 — after Cuomo resigned from office — it did not constitute acting “under color of state law.” The woman, known in court documents as Trooper 1, alleged in the lawsuit that Cuomo sexually harassed her and that his former top aides subsequently retaliated against her. The former governor has denied any wrongdoing. “We respectfully disagree with the Court's decision,” said Valdi Licul, Trooper 1’s lawyer. “Multiple federal and state agencies found that Cuomo sexually harassed Trooper 1 and other women. We don’t believe his resignation in response to his proven misconduct permitted him to further violate the law by threatening one of his victims. We intend to appeal as soon as we are able.” Azzopardi, Cuomo’s spokesperson, responded: “Despite what Trooper 1’s attorneys may think, New Yorkers aren’t stupid, they know Governor Cuomo never harassed nor retaliated against anyone and a simple review of the facts by the courts is why their case continues to crumble, the same way 5 DA’s review of those same ‘agency reviews’ found no there there and the two civil cases against him were ultimately dropped.” — Nick Reisman FROM CITY HALL FINAL FRONTIER FEAR: At least one of the artificial intelligence firms set to testify before the City Council is supportive of the lawmakers’ regulatory efforts. Council Speaker Julie Menin plans to convene the entire body Monday for a hearing where leading AI companies will testify and provide input on a legislative package that would put guardrails around the emerging technology. In a letter sent Thursday to Menin and her colleagues — and obtained by Playbook — an executive from OpenAI said the firm is broadly behind the Council’s push. “We appreciate the Council’s focus on frontier safety, including transparency, third-party assessments, reporting of critical incidents and protecting whistleblowers, consumer protection, election-related deepfakes, and other key safety areas,” wrote Chan Park, head of U.S. and Canada policy and partnerships for OpenAI. “We also strongly support the Council’s goal of strengthening the City’s readiness to prevent and respond to AI-related cyber threats and emergencies.” In his letter, Park noted the ways AI is contributing to advances in science and education, but acknowledged the concerns over frontier AI models raised by Menin and the company’s own executives as part of a broad unease over how rapidly the technology is advancing. Park did not get into the particulars of each Council bill, but he noted OpenAI is also supportive of a state regulatory framework known as the RAISE Act and has been providing Albany with input on tweaks to the legislation and the state’s cybersecurity efforts. “Our own safeguards are essential, but voluntary company commitments alone are not enough,” Park wrote. “Enforceable standards, independent scrutiny, and public accountability are necessary to ensure that increasingly capable AI is developed and used responsibly.” — Joe Anuta IN OTHER NEWS — FLUSHING’S FACELIFT: As plans for a new “town square” in Flushing move forward, residents have raised concerns about gentrification and displacement. articles.body: Senate Republicans are suddenly rushing to save a Senate seat in Kansas. On Friday, the Senate Leadership Fund, Senate Republicans’ top super PAC, reserved over $8 million in ads starting this weekend to prop up GOP Sen. Roger Marshall, according to tracking firm AdImpact. The spending in a state where Democrats haven’t won a Senate race in 94 years comes amid a deteriorating national political environment for the GOP. The impact of spiking diesel and fertilizer prices driven by the war with Iran, coupled with President Donald Trump’s trade wars, have been acutely felt in the heartland. Private polling from both parties shows a deadlocked race between Marshall and Democrat Adam Hamilton in a state Trump carried by 16 points in 2024. “It’s a perfect storm,” said one senior Senate GOP aide, granted anonymity to candidly discuss the race. “The president isn’t making it any better.” Lower Costs Now, a new Super PAC affiliated with former Vice President Kamala Harris’ Super PAC, dropped about $700,000 into the state Thursday night, and Democrats are considering more spending to bolster Hamilton. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has been including Kansas in private fundraising pitches to donors, according to two people familiar with the conversations. It’s a remarkable shift in a state that was not high on either party’s target list just a few months ago — and shows the ferocity of the headwinds Republicans face in the final month of the campaign. “I think we're on track to win, but I am comforted to know that the cavalry is coming,” said Danedri Herbert, chair of the Kansas Republican Party. Herbert said Hamilton’s particular appeal as a pastor who heads the largest United Methodist church in the country, located in suburban Kansas City, made him formidable. “I personally know people who attend or have attended that church in the past,” said Herbert. “The ones that I know are right-leaning, and so that's troublesome. That's trouble — just the sheer ability to reach some of those people who are just always our people. I was telling national groups early on, like, ‘you should pay attention here.’” Republicans say the warning signs have been visible in Kansas for months as the agriculture-heavy state got hammered by a series of economic blows, including increased input prices from Trump’s tariffs, high fuel prices as a result of the Iran war, his decision to increase foreign beef imports , and heavy-handed immigration enforcement . As diesel prices shot up just ahead of the peak harvest season, the situation started to deteriorate even more in Kansas, according to Republicans. Vice President JD Vance visited Olathe, Kansas, in mid-September to campaign with Marshall, a sign of the GOP’s growing worries. Days later, he took a shot at Hamilton during a speech in western Iowa for having “kind of a ‘gee whiz, I’m a nice pastor’ vibe,” but said he “tells his congregation not about the gospel of Jesus Christ, but that they need to repent for their white privilege while eating beef” — a reference to a frequent attack line on Hamilton about his past calls to decrease carbon emissions . Marshall recently criticized the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement, saying recent ICE operations in western Kansas should have coordinated with local law enforcement. A handful of recent public polls have shown a close race in recent weeks. Hamilton’s internal polling and a recent poll for the Democratic Attorneys General Association shared with POLITICO found him tied or up a few points against Marshall. Republicans’ numbers are no better: One Republican involved in the race said a recent private GOP poll had Marshall down within the margin of error and said Trump’s approval rating has been underwater since summer in the state; another person said a different GOP poll of Kansas found a tied Senate race. “I take it as a compliment that the Republicans are now going, ‘Oh my gosh, we didn't think we were going to have to put money into Kansas, and now we're going to pour millions of dollars in to try to save Roger Marshall,’” said Hamilton in an interview on The Conversation with Dasha Burns , published Friday. “And I don't think they're going to save him.” SLF’s Kansas ad buy came as they pulled back in North Carolina — the latest sign of a deteriorating national political environment. And the agriculture-heavy Midwest has been particularly impacted by Trump’s policies. Republicans are currently fighting to hold onto Senate, House and governor’s seats in red-leaning Iowa and Ohio, and even redder Nebraska and Kansas. Retiring GOP Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.) said the repeated economic blows to the Midwest were contributing to a series of tighter than comfortable races, including the Kansas Senate race. “It’s the policies and the chaos,” Bacon said. “That’s why Trump’s numbers are low. Tariffs are not popular in the Midwest and they contribute to the cost of goods.” National Republicans played down those concerns for weeks, arguing Marshall was still holding strong in polling and dispelling the belief that a Democrat could actually win the state. But privately, top Senate GOP operatives and Republican senators have been deeply worried about worsening economic conditions across the Midwest, increasing the states where they need to play defense. "He's running scared,” one western Kansas Republican, granted anonymity to speak candidly about the race, said. “I don't know if they took Hamilton for granted, but people are tired of Marshall not doing anything.” Asked for comment for this story, a spokesperson for the Marshall campaign sent a link to a New York Post article that details a $1.2 million buy for an ad that alleges Hamilton failed to report a pedophile who volunteered at Hamilton’s church’s camp; Hamilton’s campaign has previously said the attacks are false. “Adam Hamilton is a pedophile protector who would vote with Democrats like Chuck Schumer. He will never be the U.S. Senator from Kansas,” said National Republican Senatorial Committee spokesperson Samantha Cantrell. The SLF ad launching Saturday accuses Hamilton of being “a two-faced extremist,” and accuses him of “founding a radical group promoting the idea that all white people are racist.” "Adam Hamilton is running a strong campaign that’s giving a voice to Kansas families, farmers, seniors, and everyone being crushed by Roger Marshall’s toxic agenda," Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee spokesperson Monica Robinson said in a statement shared after publication. "Marshall is right to be terrified that he will lose his job in November." Hamilton spokesperson Tyson Brody referenced a New York Times report about Marshall, a former obstetrician, and his involvement in lawsuits against patients who didn’t pay past due bills as he dismissed the ad barrage on behalf of a “failing” incumbent. “With this new ad, Marshall is turning to these desperate lies and false attacks because Kansans have learned Roger Marshall had pregnant mothers arrested and jailed over small medical debts, and voted to block the release of the Epstein files,” he said. Democrats have also hammered Marshall over the amount of time his family spends in Florida, where they have a second home . Hamilton is considering a late-stage fundraising swing later this month that includes an event in Boston, according to a person familiar with the planning and granted anonymity to discuss it. Democrats are bullish about the state, but are facing a cash crunch across the map that could hinder their ability to spread money so far that it reaches Kansas. Senate Majority PAC was already “actively thinking” about whether to wade into the state, its president told POLITICO last week. Democrats are growing bullish about other Kansas races as well. Recent polling has also shown a relatively close race in the fight to replace term-limited Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly as well as for attorney general. And the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee added Kansas’ 2nd District, which Trump carried by nearly 20 points in 2024, to its extended offensive targets list Friday. “It's momentum, and that's what we're seeing across the state,” said Chris Mann, the Democratic nominee for attorney general. A spokesperson for Ty Masterson, the Republican gubernatorial candidate, pointed POLITICO to a mid-September Emerson College poll which showed their candidate leading Holscher 51% to 44%. The same poll found Hamilton leading Marshall 45% to 43%.

articles.body: Leading Republicans are pulling back from the North Carolina Senate race, sending a clear message: What was a top-tier battleground at the start of the cycle is no longer worth the money. The foremost Senate GOP super PAC, Senate Leadership Fund, is pausing its future spending in North Carolina and instead launching a seven-figure ad buy in deep-red Kansas, according to one person familiar with the move. The news was first reported by Semafor . The dramatic change in strategy — less than four weeks before the midterms — comes after SLF previously spent more than $30 million to boost GOP nominee Michael Whatley. It also comes as public polling has continued to show Whatley unable to close the gap against popular former Gov. Roy Cooper, the Democratic candidate. Republicans are now deprioritizing a state that President Donald Trump carried in all three presidential runs, and that Democrats haven’t won in the Senate since 2008. “We are all clear-eyed about where North Carolina stands,” said one national GOP operative working on Senate races, who like others in this article was granted anonymity to speak candidly. SLF isn’t the only major GOP group shifting away from North Carolina as Republicans focus on other must-win seats and deep-red states, amid the Iran war, high fuel prices and other economic fallout of the war in Iran. Earlier Friday, the Koch-aligned Americans for Prosperity Action left North Carolina off its $22 million list of future spending across key Senate contests, as POLITICO reported . Another major Republican group focused specifically on boosting Whatley — Old North Action — removed $6.5 million in ad reservations from North Carolina’s Senate race last month. “Michael Whatley is a good man who took one for the team — but with states like Alaska, Kansas, and Texas requiring continued resource commitments, there is only so much,” said another national GOP operative working on midterm races. “Especially against a very popular former Governor in Roy Cooper.” The National Republican Senatorial Committee is currently running coordinated ad reservations with six of its battleground candidates. Whatley in North Carolina is not one of them, according to data from advertising tracking service AdImpact. NRSC regional press secretary Nick Puglia said in a statement that “Whatley will put North Carolina families first by cutting taxes and keeping criminals locked up.” Whatley for months has struggled to boost his name ID against the much better-known Cooper. Some recent public polls show Cooper leading Whatley by double-digit margins. Private polling has also hardly budged, despite the recent influx of spending, according to a person working on the race. Trump on Friday told reporters he was "worried" about Whatley, his handpicked candidate in the battleground race. "He's a great man, and I am worried about him. I hope he wins," Trump said. "He's a great man, he was a great leader for the whole Republican Party when I won, and he'd be a great senator." In a statement, Whatley spokesperson DJ Griffin said the team feels “confident we have the resources” to win in November. “Roy Cooper recently said about federal elections in North Carolina, ‘Democrats are often ahead until they are not,’” Griffin said. “Undecided Voters who break late decide the election in North Carolina and the majority of those Late-Breakers typically go Republican.” AFP Action and Old North Action did not immediately respond to a request for comment about North Carolina. SLF declined to comment. SLF’s decision came as a shock to some, but not all, North Carolina Republicans — mostly because Senate Majority Leader John Thune has been scheduled to be in North Carolina for an event with Whatley on Thursday night. Thune ended up joining the event virtually, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. For weeks, top Republicans acknowledged North Carolina may be slipping away. One Republican who attended a donor meeting with Senate Majority Leader John Thune and SLF during the Dallas convention told POLITICO that holding the state would be “tough .” “The map has shifted a little bit, and to be fair, we knew that was going to be a tough one from the beginning," said one GOP operative working on Senate races, granted anonymity to speak candidly about the landscape. Democrats are not letting up, recognizing that the contest in the purple state could still be close. "A Democrat has not won statewide federal office here in nearly two decades, and North Carolina is a 50-50 state,” Cooper campaign manager Jeff Allen said in a statement. “We’re building a campaign to earn every vote and make sure North Carolinians know that Roy Cooper will fight for them, while Michael Whatley will continue to enrich himself at their expense,” Allen said. One North Carolina GOP strategist said that while Whatley has been a “fine” candidate, the current political climate coupled with Cooper’s long record in the state may be too much to overcome. And while Republicans have repeatedly hammered Cooper on crime, he still has strong favorability ratings from his time as governor. “He's really kind of hard to paint as a radical, 'cause, you know, he's like Aunt Martha. She's just been there forever. And so it's just very difficult to get any traction on that, because, you know, people say, 'well, Roy's okay,’” they said. When told that SLF was moving money from North Carolina to Kansas, the strategist responded: “$6.50 diesel fuel will kick your ass.”

articles.body: WORKING OUT THE KINKS: New York’s Department of Health began transitioning more than 147,000 Medicaid and Medicare Savings Program enrollees to an upgraded case management system about a year ago. Since then, state officials say only a third of them have been able to automatically renew their coverage without assistance. The shift is part of a $1.1 billion contract aimed at creating an automated system for Medicaid enrollees to receive real-time determinations on their eligibility for the two programs. While the new system is intended to create a seamless enrollment process, for many consumers it’s been riddled with challenges. The initiative is part of a broader effort to move the Medicaid program away from local social services departments that still rely on paper applications and an outdated system in desperate need of overhaul. The state wants to transition the program to one centralized system run through its public health insurance marketplace, New York State of Health, according to officials. Lindsay Heckler, managing attorney for policy at the nonprofit Center for Elder Law & Justice, said her firm has seen a surge in inappropriate denials. “I’m not saying the new system shouldn’t be in place,” Heckler said. “But the concern is that the training and processes that are in place are preventing people from becoming eligible. My concern is that in the coming year they are moving more people into a system that doesn’t have the kinks worked out for the people that are in the system right now.” The state began rolling out the new Medicaid Eligibility and Client Management system in September 2025. A second wave of more complex cases is expected to migrate to the new system between November 2027 and February 2028. And while state officials say the system — which was created by Deloitte Consulting through a $1.1 billion contract — was thoroughly tested by both the Health Department and the company, they concede that problems remain and are being addressed as they’re flagged. Advocates describe the situation in starker terms. They say errors have put health care coverage in jeopardy for people who are 65 years and older, blind or disabled. They also told POLITICO they’ve discovered inaccurate information being transferred, a flawed automated asset verification tool and state workers’ inability to manually override inappropriate denials. Deloitte did not respond to a request for comment. New York entered into a $177 million contract with Deloitte in August 2023. But that projected outlay has grown to $1.18 billion after the state quietly filed four amendments to the initial deal, which ended on March 31, 2025. The latest amendment included an $866 million extension along with a work plan modification, according to details of the contract listed in the Open Book New York database. The Health Department said the contract extension will complete the migration of Medicaid enrollees to the new system, which includes more complex cases in the next wave, such as long-term care and nursing home patients. The contract also includes additional funding for Deloitte to conduct testing and ensure compliance with new federal requirements. “This multi-year transition to a centrally administered model will replace the outdated, expensive, error-prone and inefficient paper-based system with a streamlined, user-friendly platform that better supports the health coverage needs of New Yorkers while reducing the potential for waste, fraud, and abuse,” Health Department spokesperson Cadence Acquaviva said in a statement. “At every step of the way, this transition and contract were subject to extensive federal review and approval by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.” R ead more in POLITICO Pro from Katelyn Cordero.  MARK YOUR CALENDAR: Join POLITICO’s New York Outlook: Affordability, Industry & The Economy on Oct. 14 for live conversations about the business and policy decisions being made today — from City Hall to the State Capitol — that will shape the city’s economic future. The lineup includes New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin, New York City Economic Development Corp. CEO Anthony Shorris, Partnership for NYC CEO Steven Fulop, Citizens Budget Commission President Andrew Rein, Charles H. Revson Foundation President Maria Torres-Springer, and more. Register now to attend in person or watch the livestream . From the Capitol JACOBS WINS: State Democratic Committee Chair Jay Jacobs handily won a new two-year term on the job, receiving 82 percent of the weighted vote at a party gathering in Westchester today. Jacobs — who angered the left last year by declining to endorse then-Democratic mayoral nominee Zohran Mamdani in the general election — faced a challenge from Otsego County chair Caitlin Ogden. He preached unity as his victory message, inviting Ogden to join his leadership team in a “substantive” role. “This party has got to come to an understanding that our first priority is electing Democrats in whatever districts they’re in, and speak the language of the people in those districts,” Jacobs said. “All sides of our party need to learn to listen, to understand, to respect each other. There should be no vitriol inside the Democratic Party tent.” Party members have traditionally supported the governor’s choice for chair. Gov. Kathy Hochul never publicly wavered in her support for Jacobs, making clear in recent weeks he was still her pick. “I want to thank him for accepting the weight, the responsibilities,” she told party officials today. “Not the easiest job in the state. But he has done it in a way that has brought us together.” Jacobs, who also heads the Nassau County Democratic Committee, has chaired the state party under the past three governors, serving from 2009-2012 and since 2019. If he completes his new two-year stint, he’d be just one term away from surpassing FDR kingmaker James Farley as the longest-tenured chair in the history of the New York Democrats. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL POLL POSITION: Republican Rep. Mike Lawler and Democratic challenger Cait Conley are locked in a tight race, per a new Emerson College/PIX11 poll . Conley earned 48% of support to Lawler’s 46%, with 7% of respondents undecided. Lawler has more crossover support than Conley does, and independents break for him. But the pollsters note the percentage of Democratic backing for him fell from an Emerson survey in October 2024, while Conley’s GOP support increased compared to Lawler’s 2024 opponent, former Rep. Mondaire Jones. Hochul’s favorability is underwater in the district — 40% of respondents approve and 49% disapprove — though the pollsters acknowledge she’s on better footing than she was in 2024. President Donald Trump is also unpopular, with 43% approving his performance and 53% disapproving. The poll did not ask about Mamdani, a favorite foil of Lawler’s on the trail. The survey was conducted among 400 likely voters from Sept. 27-29. It has a margin of error of plus-or-minus 4.9 percentage points. — Madison Fernandez TRUMP TO CNY: Trump is considering a trip to upstate New York on Oct. 9 to appear alongside Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman, according to three people with knowledge of the discussions. The event is being considered for central New York, but has not been finalized, said a fourth person. The people were granted anonymity to disclose the private conversations about the potential trip. Blakeman’s campaign did not comment and the White House did not immediately return messages seeking comment. Trump previously appeared on Long Island this summer to rally with Blakeman and Republican House candidates. Read more from POLITICO’s Nick Reisman. FROM CITY HALL BILLIONAIRE’S ZO: Mamdani hosted fifteen business leaders — several of them billionaires — at Gracie Mansion yesterday for the inaugural meeting of his Business Advisory Council. The council brings together business executives across industries to help guide the city’s economic policy and shepherd growth and innovation. Despite decrying the ultra wealthy, Mamdani welcomed input from billionaires such as Chobani founder and CEO Hamdi Ulukaya and Jefferson River Capital Chairman Tony James on how to address the affordability crisis, which has inhibited their ability to recruit top talent. The council also discussed potential plans to convert unused office space across the city into arts and research hubs, according to a spokesperson for the mayor. While he was welcoming other business execs to his home, one of the mayor’s biggest billionaire foes, Ken Griffin, was announcing his $3 billion donation to Carnegie Mellon University , the largest single donation in the history of American higher education. Most of that money is earmarked to build the university a new campus in Miami — months after Griffin said the mayor’s rhetoric prompted him to “double down” on investments in Florida, rather than New York. The Mamdani-Griffin beef swelled this spring when the mayor posed in front of Griffin’s $238 million penthouse in a social media video promoting his pied-à-terre tax. In the post, Mamdani framed the billionaire as a prime target of his tax-the-rich agenda. Griffin responded by calling the video “creepy and weird,” saying his plans to further invest outside of New York were “an immediate and direct consequence of the mayor’s poor decision.” “We will welcome anyone's support, anyone's involvement, and we will always do so because this is a city that belongs to all who live here,” Mamdani said when asked about Griffin’s historic donation. — Molly Reinmann IN OTHER NEWS — RETREAT: NYC first lady Rama Duwaji reportedly sojourned at an Islamic wellness retreat with a history of calling for the destruction of Israel, as her husband was rolling out his blueprint to combat antisemitism. ( Washington Free Beacon ) — CHATBOT GOVERNANCE: The Mamdani administration is planning to unroll new AI safeguards, including cracking down on chatbots used in customer service and launching a formal study of AI assistants. ( POLITICO Pro ) — SPEEDING THINGS UP: Mamdani’s administration unveiled 12 districts where housing will be fast-tracked. ( POLITICO Pro ) Missed this morning’s New York Playbook? We forgive you. "></img><p>Dos migrantes marroquíes de 22 y 25 años que dormían en los asentamientos informales de playa Benítez, en Ceuta, han relatado a EL PAÍS que el pasado martes regresaron a Marruecos porque un traductor de la Policía les dijo que la decisión de devolverles al país vecino “ya se había tomado” y que nadie les ofreció la posibilidad de pedir protección internacional, ni les tomaron información o huellas. “No me preguntaron si quería volver a Marruecos. Me arrojaron en contra de mi voluntad”, mantiene el joven de 25 años. “Nos condujeron hasta entregarnos al Ejército marroquí”, añade el de 22 años. Los migrantes llevaban en la ciudad autónoma <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-30/ceuta-dos-meses-despues-una-ciudad-paralizada-entre-la-expulsion-y-el-retorno-de-los-migrantes.html#?rel=mas" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-30/ceuta-dos-meses-despues-una-ciudad-paralizada-entre-la-expulsion-y-el-retorno-de-los-migrantes.html#?rel=mas">desde la entrada masiva del pasado 30 y 31 de julio</a> y creían que les iban a trasladar a un centro de acogida temporal del Gobierno. Sin embargo, aseguran que terminaron en la frontera y horas después metidos en un autobús, con miembros del Ejército marroquí, que los dejaron a cientos de kilómetros de la ciudad autónoma. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-03/dos-migrantes-marroquies-aseguran-que-los-forzaron-a-salir-de-ceuta-nos-dijeron-que-ya-se-habia-tomado-la-decision-de-devolvernos.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Dos migrantes marroquíes aseguran que los forzaron a salir de Ceuta: “Nos dijeron que ya se había tomado la decisión de devolvernos”

articles.body: <p>Pablo Bustinduy (Madrid, 43 años) atiende a EL PAÍS nada más acabar el pleno del Congreso que ha <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-02/el-debate-de-los-decretos-se-convierte-en-un-juicio-demoledor-contra-junts.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-02/el-debate-de-los-decretos-se-convierte-en-un-juicio-demoledor-contra-junts.html">derogado este viernes los dos decretos</a> sobre vivienda. El ministro de Derechos Sociales, encargado de defender en el hemiciclo el texto que recogía la prórroga automática de los contratos de alquiler, se reconoce cansado, después de un trabajo intenso las últimas semanas. Pero cuando responde, no escatima en palabras y deja clara su indignación por el voto en contra de las derechas. “La posición de Junts es un suicidio político”, sostiene. No se pronuncia sobre si el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, debe convocar elecciones, pero advierte de que los comicios serán “un referéndum sobre la vivienda”. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-03/pablo-bustinduy-las-elecciones-cuando-sean-van-a-ser-un-referendum-sobre-la-vivienda.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/AMEOLSLK3NHVPP5LTY6HTFOLNY.JPG?auth=c3a54bf9d4b7a50633f28e7c8cdf819b436dd7bc86ed94a53216c6a9dd26bf76" width="5671" height="3781" alt="El ministro de Derechos Sociales, Consumo y Agenda 2030, en el Congreso."></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/QZG2IAXMZNEODMIHZR2BTQYSDY.JPG?auth=1323a3a89b4268461c558e05faaa84f75c2fb2bbdcda01bb84ee650d5ff26ebe" width="5268" height="3512" alt="Pablo Bustinduy en el Congreso."></img>

articles.body: <p>Miriam Nogueras hizo un viaje relámpago de Madrid a Barcelona el miércoles. Estaba invitada a la gala que Pimec, la patronal catalana de la pequeña y mediana empresa, organiza cada año en el Palau Sant Jordi. La cena se celebraba horas después de que el presidente del Gobierno Pedro Sánchez declarara sentirse <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-30/los-socios-de-izquierda-presionan-a-podemos-para-que-permita-los-decretos-de-vivienda-como-punto-de-partida.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-30/los-socios-de-izquierda-presionan-a-podemos-para-que-permita-los-decretos-de-vivienda-como-punto-de-partida.html">“razonablemente optimista”</a> de cara a poder validar en el Congreso, este viernes, los dos decretos de vivienda que había diseñado su Consejo de Ministros. En un momento de visible crispación social, con movilizaciones en la calle, el precio del metro cuadrado ardiendo y la <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-27/diseccion-del-desahucio-de-maricarmen-podria-haber-sido-diferente.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-27/diseccion-del-desahucio-de-maricarmen-podria-haber-sido-diferente.html">crudeza de los desahucios</a> acaparando foco informativo, Nogueras lanzó un puñado de dudas al aire cuando se le preguntó si Junts votaría a favor del nuevo marco normativo: “No tenemos ningún miedo de quemarnos para continuar defendiendo los intereses de las familias catalanas”. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/catalunya/2026-10-03/junts-se-vuelca-en-su-ideario-conservador-para-protegerse-de-las-criticas-por-vetar-el-decreto.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Junts se vuelca en su ideario conservador para protegerse de las críticas por vetar el decreto

articles.body: <p>El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha decidido tomarse un tiempo, aún no definido, para pronunciarse sobre una decisión estratégica clave que solo le compete a él: qué día serán las próximas elecciones generales. La última vez, Sánchez determinó la convocatoria en pocas horas, en cuanto vio el pésimo resultado de la izquierda en las autonómicas y municipales de 2023. Lo vio claro, se lanzó y le salió bien, porque logró seguir en La Moncloa contra todo pronóstico. Pero esta vez todo indica que se va a tomar algo más de tiempo, porque la decisión de convocar ahora elecciones, en plena ola de indignación progresista frente a la derecha de PP, Vox y Junts, que tumbaron el decreto que impediría desahucios como el de Maricarmen, tiene pros y contras. Como subrayan fuentes de La Moncloa, todo abierto y nadie puede descartar “ninguna opción”. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-02/dirigentes-del-psoe-y-ministros-del-gobierno-creen-que-sanchez-debe-convocar-elecciones-si-se-tumban-los-decretos.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/USQFXA4UTFBDJNPOLK6K45MA5U.jpg?auth=9f170405e6f9191f048697cc3620bf8a53b338df0f0419bbeece69b1c9790d8b" width="5019" height="3124" alt="El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, entra en el hemiciclo acompañado por la ministra de Vivienda, Isabel Rodríguez, este viernes. "></img>

articles.body: <p>Ante la disyuntiva entre un <a href="https://elpais.com/economia/vivienda/2026-10-01/la-compra-de-viviendas-cae-un-7-en-el-segundo-trimestre-respecto-al-ano-pasado-y-confirma-la-desaceleracion-del-mercado.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/economia/vivienda/2026-10-01/la-compra-de-viviendas-cae-un-7-en-el-segundo-trimestre-respecto-al-ano-pasado-y-confirma-la-desaceleracion-del-mercado.html">mercado de la vivienda</a> que se regula a sí mismo en base a la oferta y la demanda o una intervención del Estado para fijar reglas a costa del lucro privado, en la sociedad española se impone con claridad la segunda opción. Es decir, se imponen las visiones dominantes en los principales partidos de izquierdas. Pero no solo ganan entre los votantes progresistas, también entre quienes respaldan al PP y Vox, aunque por menos distancia. Así lo pone de relieve la encuesta sobre vivienda de <a href="https://40db.es/" rel="">40dB.</a> para EL PAÍS y la Cadena SER elaborada con 2.000 entrevistas <i>online </i>entre el 25 de septiembre, dos días después del <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-23/maricarmen-se-queda-un-centenar-de-activistas-espera-junto-a-la-anciana-a-la-comision-judicial.html" rel="">desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal</a>, y el 28 de septiembre, un día antes de que el Ejecutivo <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-29/el-gobierno-aprueba-la-proteccion-frente-a-los-desahucios-hasta-2030-y-la-prorroga-de-los-contratos-de-alquiler-hasta-2028.html?outputType=amp" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-29/el-gobierno-aprueba-la-proteccion-frente-a-los-desahucios-hasta-2030-y-la-prorroga-de-los-contratos-de-alquiler-hasta-2028.html?outputType=amp">aprobara los dos decretos</a> con los que ha intentado dar una respuesta urgente a la conmoción social suscitada por el caso.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-02/la-intervencion-para-bajar-el-alquiler-arrasa-en-la-izquierda-y-se-impone-tambien-entre-los-votantes-del-pp-y-vox.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, se ha adelantado a la incertidumbre que deja el pleno extraordinario de este viernes sobre <a href="https://elpais.com/videos/2026-10-02/la-comparecencia-integra-de-pedro-sanchez-en-el-congreso-por-los-decretos-de-vivienda.html?autoplay=1" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/videos/2026-10-02/la-comparecencia-integra-de-pedro-sanchez-en-el-congreso-por-los-decretos-de-vivienda.html?autoplay=1">los próximos pasos del presidente del Gobierno</a> y la posibilidad de una convocatoria electoral. Tras la derrota parlamentaria del Ejecutivo, Feijóo ha reclamado elecciones y ha lanzado un mensaje directo a Sánchez: “Hoy se ha acreditado que Sánchez y su Gobierno no tienen ni las Cortes ni las calles”, ha sostenido en una comparecencia tras el pleno. “La única salida decente y democrática es la convocatoria de elecciones. Que no se guarde mucho más la fecha ante la eventualidad de pillar a la oposición desprevenida. Estamos preparados. Por mí, que convoque cuando quiera”, ha espetado.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-02/feijoo-reta-a-sanchez-a-convocar-elecciones-tras-el-reves-de-los-decretos-estamos-preparados.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Feijóo reta a Sánchez a convocar elecciones tras el revés de los decretos: “Estamos preparados”

articles.body: <p>Tenía casas de lujo en Madrid, Ibiza y Dubái. Entre sus empresas había promotoras inmobiliarias, compañías de compraventa de vehículos de alta gama e, incluso, negocios de hidrocarburos. Lucía ostentosos relojes en la muñeca, se desplazaba en automóviles exclusivos y pasaba largas temporadas en su residencia en la isla balear o en una vivienda en el emirato sin reparar en gastos. A sus 51 años, nunca había sido detenido ni acusado formalmente de ningún delito, aunque su nombre ―que no ha transcendido públicamente― llevaba apareciendo en investigaciones policiales desde hace al menos 10 años. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-02/cae-un-empresario-acusado-de-levantar-villas-de-lujo-en-ibiza-y-marbella-para-blanquear-fortunas-de-grandes-narcos.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>La jueza de Catarroja (Valencia) que investiga la dana, Nuria Ruiz Tobarra, ha rechazado investigar por falso testimonio <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/comunidad-valenciana/2026-09-21/la-jueza-de-la-dana-descarta-un-careo-entre-dos-dirigentes-del-pp.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/comunidad-valenciana/2026-09-21/la-jueza-de-la-dana-descarta-un-careo-entre-dos-dirigentes-del-pp.html">al diputado responsable del área de bomberos de la Diputación de Valencia, Avelino Mascarell (PP)</a>, tal y como solicitaba una de las acusaciones. En un auto divulgado este viernes, la magistrada justifica que, al no existir sentencia firme ni concluido la instrucción de la causa —que desde hace dos años rastrea la responsabilidad penal de la riada que dejó 233 muertos en Valencia en octubre de 2024— no se puede situar bajo el foco de las pesquisas a Mascarell. El falso testimonio contempla penas de hasta dos años de cárcel para el testigo que mienta en una instrucción, según el artículo 458 del Código Penal. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/comunidad-valenciana/2026-10-02/la-jueza-de-la-dana-rechaza-investigar-a-un-diputado-del-pp-por-falso-testimonio.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Junts expresó su rechazo al decreto de vivienda a las puertas de la votación hoy en el Congreso. Sin embargo, los independentistas esta vez no pueden apelar a que no han estado en la negociación y elaboración del decreto, porque el texto, según algunas fuentes del Gobierno, tiene su impronta en un porcentaje muy elevado, que algunos cifran incluso en un 80%. La ministra de Vivienda, Isabel Rodríguez, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-01/podemos-anuncia-su-apoyo-a-los-decretos-de-vivienda-en-el-congreso.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-01/podemos-anuncia-su-apoyo-a-los-decretos-de-vivienda-en-el-congreso.html">lleva meses negociando de forma discreta con Junts y con todos los demás grupos</a>, en especial el PNV, el otro hueso duro de roer porque tiene muchas discrepancias ideológicas sobre la política de vivienda del Gobierno. No en vano ni Junts ni PNV votaron a favor de la ley de vivienda aprobada en la anterior legislatura con el apoyo de la izquierda, porque no estaban de acuerdo.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-02/un-decreto-cosido-a-medida-para-implicar-a-toda-la-mayoria.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

"></img><p>Junts per Catalunya rechaza validar los dos decretos de vivienda que el Gobierno <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-01/calculadora-de-votos-saldra-adelante-el-decreto-de-vivienda-simule-las-votaciones-por-partidos.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-01/calculadora-de-votos-saldra-adelante-el-decreto-de-vivienda-simule-las-votaciones-por-partidos.html">llevará al Congreso de los Diputados este viernes</a>. El partido independentista catalán ha estado evaluando internamente qué posicionamiento adoptaba en un asunto que tiene la consideración de material altamente sensible y ha hecho público el desenlace entrada la noche de este jueves. A pesar del clamor de las calles, los independentistas han pedido retirar los decretos y acelerar un nuevo redactado, alegando que las medidas incorporadas en el texto actual “provocarán el efecto contrario”, es decir, reducirán la oferta de alquiler y encarecerán aún más los precios. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/catalunya/2026-10-01/junts-acuerda-tumbar-los-dos-decretos-de-vivienda-del-gobierno.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: L’Auditori ha inaugurat temporada amb la seva formació resident, l’ Orquestra Simfònica de Barcelona i Nacional de Catalunya , considerada una de les principals formacions simfòniques de l’estat espanyol amb Ludovic Morlot al capdavant. Un concert amb les entrades gairebé exhaurides que tenia com a principal reclam la Simfonia número 7 de Beethoven. Però ha estat el Concertino per a orquestra de corda del català Robert Gerhard la peça que ha encetat el concert inaugural. Escrita el 1927 i el 1928, combina el diàleg amb la tradició amb la recerca d’un llenguatge modern . Considerat un dels compositors catalans més importants del segle XX, se li dedica la Biennal Robert Gerhard a Barcelona i Valls i aquest concert ha estat el primer del programa. Ludovic Morlot, director de l’OBC També et pot interessar L’OBC obre la temporada a L’Auditori amb la ‘Setena’ de Beethoven Mercè Alsina 3 minuts de lectura Reivindicar la clàssica catalana El director de l’OBC, Ludovic Morlot ha explicat a betevé que “tenia moltes ganes de començar la temporada amb música catalana” i ha confessat que “ Robert Gerhard és un compositor que m’interessa molt i de qui actualment treballo en un enregistrament amb l’orquestra”. Ha avançat que a finals d’any es publicarà un àlbum de Gerhard amb el seu concert per a violí i la simfonia Nova York . El programa l’ha seguit el Concert per a piano i orquestra número 2 de Frédéric Chopin , que ha combinat el lirisme i la introspecció amb passatges de gran virtuosisme protagonitzat pel pianista canadenc Jan Lisiecki com a solista. Ha tancat el concert l’esperada Simfonia número 7 , una de les obres mestres més aclamades de Beethoven . Un programa que es repetirà aquest diumenge, 4 d’octubre. També et pot interessar Ludovic Morlot: “L’OBC és una orquestra espontània, que toca amb el cor” Javier Arilla 2 minuts de lectura “Una orquestra millorada” Després de cinc anys al capdavant de l’OBC, Ludovic Morlot explica que la formació ha millorat: “És una orquestra que ha evolucionat en la seva eficàcia de treball, la seva versatilitat; és una orquestra que pot canviar d’estil molt ràpidament “. El director explica que aquesta evolució es deu, en gran part, als enregistraments i a les gires, que han permès conèixer-se per evolucionar cap a una direcció comuna. L’OBC enceta una programació ambiciosa Amb aquest concert, l’OBC inaugura la primera temporada a L’Auditori amb Víctor Medem com a director. Proposa un repertori extens que combinen llegat i descoberta , i en què els compositors Strauss , Wagner , Šostakovič , Beethoven i Rakhmaninov tindran un paper destacat. articles.body: Una malaltia intestinal, un càncer o una lesió poden fer necessari recórrer a una ostomia . Es tracta d’una intervenció quirúrgica que crea una obertura a l’abdomen on s’hi connecta una bossa. La seva funció principal és permetre la sortida dels residus corporals (femta o orina) quan el cos no ho pot fer de manera natural. Per als pacients això implica aprendre a conviure amb una nova realitat i adaptar-se als canvis físics , emocionals i socials . També et pot interessar Un lavabo accessible per a persones amb ostomia, a l’aeroport del Prat També et pot interessar Aprendre a viure amb una bossa “Al principi és un trauma, però a dia d’avui faig totes les coses que pensava que deixaria de fer, com viatjar o fer senderisme”, explica l’Eugeni, que conviu amb una ostomia urinària des de fa dos anys. Per ajudar a pacients com ell, la Fundació Puigvert ha inaugurat un nou programa d’ Aula Pacient de formació, suport i acompanyament per a persones que viuen amb una urostomia. Aquesta iniciativa consta d’una trobada presencial mensual fins al mes de juny, amb un equip multidisciplinar. En aquest sentit, la Mireia Plans , una de les infermeres que coordina el programa, apunta que durant les trobades s’aborden aspectes clínics , com la preparació abans de la cirurgia, la cura de l’ostomia i de la pell, però també factors com “l’ alimentació , el benestar emocional, la sexualitat o la vida social i laboral, entre d’altres”. També et pot interessar El pacient trasplantat de ronyó número 3.000 a la Fundació Puigvert: “La meva dona em va salvar” Sandra García Prat 1 minut de lectura L’urostomia i les seves causes Malgrat que a Espanya no hi ha un registre oficial de pacients amb una ostomia, s’estima que hi ha entre 70.000 i 100.000 persones que viuen amb un estoma; dels quals entre el 10 i el 13 % és una urostomia. La Federació d’Associacions de Persones Ostomizades d’Espanya (FAPOE) , però, eleva la xifra d’ostomitzats a 210.000 persones. El doctor Rubén Parada , especialista en Onco-urologia de la Fundació Puigvert, assegura que una de les causes principal per practirar una urostomia és el càncer de bufeta . Tot i això, aquest no és l’únic motiu: en percentatges més baixos, accidents o cops forts a la zona pelviana que causen un mal irreversible a l’aparell urinari, problemes neurològics que afecten els nervis que controlen la bufeta, malformacions o lesions causades per radioteràpia , poden fer necessaria aquesta intervenció. articles.body: El Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya ha actualitzat aquest matí els avisos per pluja molt intensa davant l’episodi que pot deixar aiguats torrencials acompanyats de tempesta durant les properes hores. A Barcelona l’avís és de perill màxim. També et pot interessar Travessar un carrer ple d’aigua un dia de pluja no és una bona idea Oriol Rodríguez Ballester 3 minuts de lectura Atenció ja durant el dia Tot i que el dissabte ha començat amb clarianes, el temps ha de ser molt inestable durant tot el que queda de dia. Les tempestes, puntualment intenses , podran entrar en qualsevol moment del dia de mar cap a terra i deixar quantitats ja importants de precipitació en poca estona. En aquest sentit, el Meteocat ha elevat l’avís ja a vermell de grau 5 sobre 6 davant la possibilitat que es puguin superar els 40 litres en 30 minuts en una franja que afecta qualsevol punt del litoral català, sobretot a partir del vespre. S’avisa, també, de la possibilitat que es puguin superar en només tres hores els 90 litres acumulats . No plourà en cap cas tot el dia, però quan ho faci ho podrà fer amb molta intensitat. Es tracta d’una situació molt complicada, que s’ha de seguir minut a minut però que en aquest primer tram s’allargarà fins entrada la nit. També et pot interessar Un mar més calent del compte fa ploure més? Oriol Rodríguez Ballester 5 minuts de lectura El moment més complicat, de nit i matinada i diumenge El moment més complicat d’aquest episodi de pluja torrencial pot arribar durant la matinada i el matí de diumenge , amb l’aproximació d’una petita baixa mediterrània que pot tenir algunes característiques de caire tropical . Són diversos els models que indiquen la possibilitat de superar els 100 i fins i tot els 200 litres per metre quadrat en poques hores en alguns trams de la costa i el prelitoral, preferentment a les comarques de Girona i Barcelona, que és on els models van insistint en què la probabilitat d’aiguats torrencials és més important. font: Meteocat El Meteocat ha actualitzat els avisos i ha elevat a grau màxim (6 sobre 6) la possibilitat alta que se superin els 40 litres en 30 minuts des de les 2 h fins a les 14 h d’aquest diumenge a Barcelona i bona part de la costa i prelitoral de Catalunya. També hi ha un avís de color vermell , de grau 5 sobre 6, davant la possibilitat que es puguin superar els 90 litres en només tres hores. Protecció Civil té un seguit de consells preventius al seu portal davant la possibilitat de pluges abundants i intenses com les que podria donar l’episodi d’aquest cap de setmana i del que aquí en tens un petit resum: Com preparar-se per un episodi de pluges? Cal que estigueu atents a les previsions meteorològiques abans que arribin les precipitacions. Cal que reviseu periòdicament la teulada . Cal que mantingueu nets els baixants i desguassos d’aigua de pluja, especialment als patis o terrats dels edificis. En situació d’emergència seguiu les indicacions de les autoritats . Informeu-vos a Twitter i Facebook de Protecció Civil i altres mitjans de comunicació. Què fer si sou en un edifici o al vostre domicili? És important que tingueu un transistor , els medicaments indispensables i la documentació personal . També cal tenir el telèfon mòbil carregat . No baixeu al soterrani ni tampoc al garatge perquè són zones que es poden inundar. Tanqueu portes i finestres i obtureu totes les escletxes possibles. Retireu mobles i objectes de l’exterior que l’aigua pugui arrossegar. articles.body: Les diferents iniciatives sorgides al voltant de la decisió referent al nom del barri de Navas han arribat a un consens. Després de mesos d’incertesa en què uns —els que volien el canvi de nom —, i d’altres —els que el volien mantenir — no sabien on anirien a parar els seus projectes, el districte ha decidit ara canalitzar-los en un de sol. Serà per la via d’un procés participatiu . Es tracta d’una eina de debat, un simple punt de partida que no generarà cap mena resultat . De fet, el districte ja ha programat decisió vinculant sobre el canvi de nom per al proper mandat. Tot i això, les parts implicades estan satisfetes: “És el que tots demanàvem”, diu Alfred Puig, membre de l’AV Torrent de la Guineu – Navas. Objectiu i format del procés Perquè el veïnat pugui decidir a les urnes el canvi de nom és necessari engegar una consulta de barri . I per encetar un procediment com aquest “és imprescindible haver fet abans un procés participatiu, i aquest és el punt actual”, explica Eva Luengo, membre de la direcció de Participació i Innovació Democràtica del districte de Sant Andreu. L’objectiu ara, doncs, és recollir les diferents opcions de nom que hi ha pel barri i explicar-les al conjunt del veïnat, fomentant un debat ciutadà amb el qual es pugui arribar al màxim nombre de persones possible. Per aconseguir-ho, hi ha previstos tres col·loquis territorials ens tres punts i hores diferents perquè el màxim nombre de veïns hi puguin assistir. D’altra banda, també s’estan preparant dues rutes pels carrers de Navas per explicar als assistents la relació històrica i toponímica de les diferents propostes amb el barri. Calendari d’actuacions Per ara, encara no hi ha data concreta per a les trobades. Els únics detalls que han trascendit són el lloc on aquestes es produiran —al centre cívic del barri, al Casal de Gent Gran i al CEM Espronceda —, així com el fet que durant aquest octubre s’acabaran de preparar les sessions, els materials i les metodologies entre els membres del grup impulsor , format per l’AV Torrent de la Guineu – Navas, l’agrupació Navas, el nostre barri, l’equip tècnic del districte i un membre de la Sindicatura de Greuges. S’espera que tot plegat conclogui de cara al gener . També et pot interessar La nova AV Navas naixerà de la divisió pel canvi de nom del barri Max Sagués 3 minuts de lectura

articles.body: La consellera de Territori, Habitatge i Transició Ecològica, Sílvia Paneque , ha defensat la proposta que ja va anunciar el president de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa , i que no té el suport del Parlament , que consisteix en la compra conjunta d’habitatge entre la Generalitat i un particular per donar estabilitat residencial als interessats i incrementar el parc de pisos protegits de Catalunya. El govern català està estudiant totes les fórmules per ampliar el parc d’habitatge protegit , tant amb obra nova com amb pisos ja existents. “És com si ja no fos només la Generalitat, els ajuntaments i el tercer sector sinó que hi hagués un exèrcit de persones, ciutadans i ciutadanes de classe mitjana que ens ajuden a adquirir aquest parc d’habitatge, del qual en aquest moment grans fons s’està desprenent”, ha expressat Paneque en un contacte amb els mitjans de comunicació. La mesura, amb una dotació inicial de 100 milions d’euros , entrarà en vigor a partir de principis del 2027 i va adreçada als majors de 40 anys amb ingressos estables però que no tenen prou diners per comprar-se un pis al mercat lliure. També et pot interessar Illa anuncia que el govern comprarà part de l’habitatge dels majors de 40 anys Redacció 2 minuts de lectura Els fons es volen desprendre dels pisos de lloguer Paneque ha explicat que, amb les mesures que limiten el preu del lloguer a Catalunya , els fons d’inversió o voltors volen desprendre’s dels actius immobiliaris del mercat de lloguer perquè ja no els donen la rendibilitat que esperaven. Per posar-ne un exemple, segons la consellera de Territori, Habitatge i Transició Ecològica, Blackstone els ha ofert 400 habitatges . Si els ciutadans participessin en aquesta operació de compra conjunta amb l’Administració, la Generalitat ampliaria el parc posant la meitat dels diners, que a més els recuperaria si al final del contracte l’interessat es quedés amb el 100 % del pis. Segons la consellera, a través del tanteig i retracte, la Generalitat en dos anys ja ha adquirit prop de 5.000 habitatges per valor de 400 milions d’euros a diversos bancs i fons voltors o d’inversió, entre els quals hi havia un paquet de 742 pisos i un altre de 1.100. També et pot interessar Barcelona o Madrid: a quina ciutat hi ha més desnonaments? Cristina Brotons 2 minuts de lectura Una proposta sense consens al Parlament El Parlament va rebutjar dijous aquesta proposta dels socialistes de crear un programa d’adquisició conjunta d’habitatge amb la Generalitat. El punt va comptar únicament amb els vots favorables del PSC i ERC , l’abstenció de Comuns i l’oposició de Junts, PPC, Vox, CUP i AC . En canvi, la cambra sí que ha reclamat un grup d’experts per a una reforma fiscal en habitatge en tres mesos —transaccional entre PSC i ERC—, tot i l’abstenció de Junts. En declaracions als mitjans després de la sessió plenària, la portaveu del govern, Sílvia Paneque, va recordar que no era la primera vegada que la cambra tombava una mesura proposada pel govern al Debat de política general i va assegurar que l’ executiu la impulsarà igualment . articles.body: En el context musical actual, el punt de connexió entre allò tradicional i allò més actual té noms i cognoms: Giulietta Vidal i Irene Romo. Elles són Alosa , sens dubte dues de les veus del moment i barcelonines, tal com reivindiquen al seu èxit ‘ Nenes de ciutat ’. View this post on Instagram A post shared by betevé (@betevecat) Si una cosa les caracteritza és la naturalitat amb què defensen i reivindiquen Barcelona. Per això, a banda de les places, asseguren que Barcelona no seria Barcelona sense les barcelonines , “per tant, que qui siguin barcelonines s’hi puguin quedar, no trobes?”, interpel·la la Giulietta a la seva companya. Saben perfectament com n’és de dur haver de marxar del teu barri. Precisament la Giulietta situa alguns dels seus records més dolços al Fort Pienc , on va créixer. És on sempre li agrada tornar, “perquè ara no visc allà, aleshores tinc moments bonics de nostàlgia i de pensar: realment s’hi viu molt bé, tant de bo pogués tornar-hi ”, explica la cantant.   Altres Barcelones La Barcelona d’Adrià Collado: “No veig una ciutat millor per viure al món, ho té tot” Mar Arans 3 minuts de lectura En canvi, segons la Irene, un dels records més dolços l’ha viscut fa poc quan es va banyar a la platja del Bogatell. “Pensava que no m’agradaria l’experiència, però va ser molt bonic”, diu sorpresa. No obstant això, també tenen alguns records amb un gust més agre, com la primera ruptura de la Irene en què pensava “com me’n sortiré, d’aquesta! I mira, soc aquí” , diu ara, rient. O l’ensurt que va viure la Giulietta un dia de nit tornant a casa: “He tingut por i això marca molt. Després no vols passar per segons quins carrers”, lamenta la cantant. Recorda, però, que aquest és un problema que, malauradament, no només afecta Barcelona.  També et pot interessar La Barcelona de Queralt Lahoz: “La Sagrada Família és el nostre imperi romà” Mar Arans 4 minuts de lectura “Gràcia sempre guanya” Coincideixen que Gràcia és el seu barri preferit . Segons la Irene, “sempre guanya”, mentre que la Giulietta, a banda de pensar-s’ho, hi afegeix amb certa resignació un: “Quin remei!”.  Per elles, el pla perfecte a Barcelona és “caminar, aparèixer a un lloc i caminar fins a un altre”. Precisament així és com va ser la millor cita de la Giulietta: “Recordo quedar a Arc de Triomf i anar baixant, baixant, baixant fins a arribar al mar i pensar: ostres, realment tenim això aquí, eh?”.  Això sí, un pla perfecte a la ciutat ha d’anar acompanyat d’un bon tiberi. Per això recorden amb afecte “ la primera vegada que ens van convidar a un restaurant per ser Alosa, ens va fer molta il·lusió ”. Expliquen que va ser al Mesa Lobo i, per com ho diuen, de ben segur que hi tornaran!  subscriu-te a l’agenda de betevé No et quedis sense plans per fer a Barcelona Neus Valls Núria Dias Sílvia Carbonell 2 minuts de lectura

articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) El Sindicat de Llogateres planteja una vaga general imminent després de la derogació dels dos decrets d’habitatge . “Tenim un congrés rendista, cal generar un conflicte molt més gros, molt més ampli, un conflicte de masses”, ha afirmat la portaveu de l’entitat, Carme Arcarazo , en declaracions als mitjans abans de l’assemblea oberta a la plaça de Catalunya, on es manté l’acampada. Arcarazo ha assegurat que parlen amb diversos sindicats laborals — CCOO, UGT i CGT — per encaminar-se cap a una aturada en els pròxims mesos . “El que hem de fer és créixer, que aquesta espurna es converteixi en una onada massiva de mobilització constant que culmini amb una vaga general que pugui transformar el sistema d’habitatge”, ha dit. També et pot interessar El Congrés dels Diputats tomba els dos decrets d’habitatge amb el no de Junts, el PP i Vox Marina Segura i Vidal 2 minuts de lectura “Caldrà una feina ingent” Arcarazo ha explicat que l’assemblea abordarà com caminar cap a una vaga general. “Una vaga general no només es convoca, sinó que una vaga general, sobretot, s’organitza”, ha dit. “ Caldrà moltíssima gent els pròxims mesos , piquets, extensió, xerrades… caldrà una feina ingent. Tot això seran alguns dels temes que podem començar a parlar des d’ara”, ha afegit. En aquest sentit, ha indicat que cal “traçar el pla”. Segons la portaveu del sindicat, que no hagi prosperat l’anomenat decret Maricarmen és només el principi. “L’espurna que s’ha encès aquesta setmana no només no acaba, sinó que s’ha de fer molt més grossa i arribar a moltes més bandes”, ha apuntat. Arcarazo ha lamentat que el Congrés dels Diputats “doni l’esquena a la ciutadania” i ha assegurat: “Això ha de canviar”.
